newsitem.title: UK: Bakychik details gold mine restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Bakychik details gold mine restructuring.

text.p: London-listed mining company Bakyrchik Gold Plc (BKG) said on Wednesday that it has restructured its ownership of the Bakyrchik mining venture.

Under the restructuring deal, Singapore-based Indochina Goldfields Ltd will buy 65 percent of the central Asian gold mine for $65 million, increasing its stake to 80 percent, and assume management of the project.

At present, the mine is 85 percent owned by BKG through its subsidiary Central Asian Mining Ltd (CAML) with the other 15 percent held by Indochina. BKG will now own 20 percent of the Kazakhstan mine and has the right to increase its ownership up to 30 percent.
BKG has also negotiated a short-term financing package, which will allow it to make a second instalment of $15 million to the government of Kazakhstan.
Following the announcement, the stock exchange lifted the suspension of BKG shares which promptly fell 28-1/2p to 55p. The company requested suspension on June 16.
However, the shares will be re-suspended as the stock exchange no longer views BKG shares as suitable for a full listing following the restructuring.
BKG said it will consider moving the company to the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) or seek a listing on another stock exchange.
